issues.title: [Bug][Ming-Omni] Video input preprocessing is incompatible with Transformers 5.x
issues.body:
## Summary

Ming-Omni video inputs fail during preprocessing on current `main`. The repository pins `transformers==5.12.1`, where `Qwen2VLImageProcessor` no longer accepts the legacy `videos=` argument used by Ming.

The failure occurs before the video encoder and Thinker run, so every Ming request containing video is currently blocked.

## Affected code

`sglang_omni/models/ming_omni/components/preprocessor.py` currently calls:

```python
result = processor.preprocess(
    images=None,
    videos=np_videos,
    return_tensors="pt",
)
```

The call was introduced with Ming video support in #471. Transformers 4.57.6 still accepted it with a deprecation warning, but Transformers 5.12.1 rejects it.

The repository directly pins Transformers 5.12.1 in `pyproject.toml` and the CPU, ROCm, NPU, and XPU dependency manifests.

## Reproduction

This reproduces on CPU and does not require the Ming checkpoint or a GPU:

```powershell
@'
import numpy as np
import transformers
from transformers import Qwen2VLImageProcessor

print("transformers:", transformers.__version__)
frames = np.zeros((2, 224, 224, 3), dtype=np.uint8)

Qwen2VLImageProcessor().preprocess(
    images=None,
    videos=[frames],
    return_tensors="pt",
)
'@ | docker run --rm -i --entrypoint python \
  hongccc/sglang-omni@sha256:02a85f00438c901c72a2eb2ef738974a807f63af3d13084445604f3344067b19 -
```

Actual result:

```text
transformers: 5.12.1
TypeError: Qwen2VLImageProcessorKwargs.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'videos'
```

## Expected behavior

Ming video frames should be converted into `pixel_values_videos` and `video_grid_thw`, then continue through the image/video encoder and Thinker.

## Proposed direction

Transformers 5.x provides a separate `Qwen2VLVideoProcessor`. Ming should use it for video while retaining `Qwen2VLImageProcessor` for images.

Because `ensure_video_list_async` already decodes, resizes, and samples frames, the video processor should be invoked with `do_sample_frames=False` to avoid sampling a second time.

A local proof using `tests/data/draw.mp4` produced:

```text
video_grid_thw: [[4, 36, 64]]
pixel_values_videos.shape: (9216, 1536)
video token count: 2304
```

The grid and tensor shape match the former Transformers 4.57.6 video-processing contract. This verifies preprocessing compatibility only; complete real-model video-to-text inference still requires separate GPU validation.

| Dataset revision | `27f4c1adee83b5b29b7c4b375f6b976324bda308` |
| Config | `examples/configs/s2pro_tts.yaml` |
| Benchmark | `benchmarks/eval/benchmark_tts_seedtts.py` |
| Provider | Modal classic Sandbox |
| Hardware | Exactly one H100 80 GB, 16 physical CPU cores, 65,536 MiB RAM |
| GPU/driver/CUDA | H100 80 GB / 580.95.05 / 13.0.3 |
| Key packages | torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1, sglang 0.5.18, flashinfer 0.6.17, py-spy 0.4.2 |
| Cost constraint | Credits only, confirmed before allocation |
| Local raw evidence | `.profiling-runs/fishaudio_s2_pro/` (gitignored) |

Preflight started at 0% GPU utilization, 4 MiB memory, and zero compute rows. Repository/network/Volume access, launch-mode py-spy, server readiness, and a real one-sample voice-cloning request all succeeded. Direct post-hoc py-spy attach is forbidden by Modal isolation, so profiling servers were launched underneath py-spy.

The benchmark regime was warmed, disjoint-shard traffic with natural duplicate-reference reuse. Each mode received an uncounted 32-request load with 16 script warmups before discovery measurements.

## Layer 1 — GPU busy ratio

Headline load: 128 requests at concurrency 16 per mode, tightly bracketed by 0.2-second `nvidia-smi` sampling. A separate torch trace measured the union of kernel/memcpy/memset intervals.

| Metric | Non-streaming | Streaming |
|---|---:|---:|
| Completed / failed | 128 / 0 | 128 / 0 |
| Mean latency | 7.187 s | 7.212 s |
| p95 / p99 / max latency | 10.142 / 10.984 / 11.850 s | 10.341 / 10.989 / 11.611 s |
| Throughput | 2.107 req/s | 2.130 req/s |
| Mean / max RTF | 2.183 / 6.4338 | 1.861 / 4.2993 |
| Mean / p95 / max audio TTFP | n/a | 6.3627 / 9.3884 / 10.0953 s |
| `nvidia-smi` samples | 257 | 247 |
| Mean / median / max GPU utilization | 51.92% / 73% / 95% | 54.02% / 77% / 90% |
| GPU activity interval union | 48.55% | 48.89% |
| Max GPU memory | 80,149 MiB | 77,773 MiB |

**Finding:** both measurement methods agree that the H100 is materially unsaturated at concurrency 16. This does not support GPU-kernel-first optimization. Evidence strength: **medium**, because each method has one clean directional run.

The latency distributions contain no runaway single request: maximum latency stays close to p99 in both modes. Streaming had zero maximum underrun among 127 continuity-eligible requests.

issues.title: [TTS][Qwen3] 1.7B variant: dedicated single-instance serving optimization
issues.body:
## Goal

Community deployments primarily use `Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base`, but the original tuning work focused on 0.6B. On one H100, the 1.7B single instance peaked at 10.26 QPS while same-card DP2+MPS reached 15.26 QPS (+49%), pointing to host-side serving overhead rather than a model-compute limit.

Exit criterion: bring single-instance peak within 95% of same-card DP2+MPS on the same silicon, with C16 EN WER within 0.2 points of baseline and TTFA p95 at c8/c16 degraded by no more than 10%, or document a profile-backed structural reason for the remaining gap.

## Validated outcome

| Silicon | Baseline single instance | Optimized single instance | Same-card DP2+MPS | Optimized gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H200 | 8.74 QPS | 12.40 QPS | 13.76 QPS | **+41.9%** |
| H100 | 10.59 QPS | 14.86 QPS | 15.61 QPS | **+40.3%**; 95.2% of pool peak |

Quality remained within the gate (H100 C16 EN WER: default 1.06%, optimized 1.11%, DP2 1.01%). The admission/queueing TTFA cliff was removed; H100 c64 TTFA p95 improved from 4.76s to 0.54s, and H200 c64 measured 1.08s.

## Completed work

- [x] **Admission, queueing, and host path:** #1413, #1449, #1462, #1649
- [x] **Benchmark and regression coverage:** #1505
- [x] **Streaming and vocoder foundation:** #1286, #1336, #1523, #1675, #1756, #1786
- [x] **Predictor and sampling optimizations:** #1641, #1726
- [x] **Evaluated NO-GO or superseded paths:** #704, #1643, #1722, #1733, #1790, #1847

## Remaining work

- [ ] **P0 — Eliminate the overload device-side assert.** Under load, an invalid codec value can reach the vocoder lookup and abort the pipeline (`vectorized_gather_kernel` index out of bounds; one observed run failed 230 requests). Use the reproducible `feat/qtts17-mask-shaping` fork branch to identify the first producer-side invalid tuple, enforce the producer invariant, and prove the signature is gone on both the accelerated repro and baseline paths.
- [ ] **P1 — Ship the confirmed 1.7B defaults.** After P0, rerun the no-compile H200 grid at c32/c64/c96 with `max_running_requests=64`, `cuda_graph_max_bs=64`, and isolated vocoder. If the throughput, WER, TTFA, VRAM, startup, and stability gates hold, update the 1.7B factory defaults. The previously measured admission-64 plus isolated-vocoder point reached 12.05 QPS versus the 8.73-QPS baseline, but it must be reconfirmed after #1649 removed Talker compile.

## Related active work

- **Awaiting review or merge:** #1554, #1625, #1640, #1642, #1757, #1794, #1848, #1853
- **Still needs benchmark or quality evidence:** #1581, #1698, #1753, #1772, #1846, #1852, #1855

NVIDIA SM-selected attention backend remains an experiment, not a completion blocker. Only pursue it if profiling shows meaningful attention cost on SM100+; any backend change requires a controlled performance A/B and the full quality gate.

General Qwen3-TTS concurrency, DP/MPS deployment, and streaming/stateful work remain tracked in #1399, #1400, #1754, and their individual PRs rather than in this 1.7B single-instance Roadmap.

issues.title: [ASR Streaming] Realtime Input Streaming Roadmap and PR Tracker
issues.body:
This is the tracker for **input streaming (live audio in) for ASR models**. New PRs should use the title prefix `[ASR Streaming]` and link this issue in the PR body.

Related trackers: #1267 (ASR refactor, shared mechanics this work builds on), #1754 (TTS roadmap, same tracking format; TTS input streaming is explicitly out of scope there and here).

## Goal

Let clients push audio incrementally over a WebSocket session and receive transcript events while the audio is still arriving, for every ASR model we serve, through **one fixed protocol**. Today `/v1/audio/transcriptions` only accepts a complete file (optionally with SSE output streaming); live captioning, voice agents and telephony need to send audio as it is captured.

## Design principles

1. **Protocol first.** Models adapt to the protocol, not the other way around. A model that can't do something natively declares it; we never bend the wire contract for one model's limitation.
2. **Target OpenAI Realtime GA (transcription intent).** Beta was retired in May 2026 and no current SDK speaks it. The existing `/v1/realtime` conversation session (#385) migrates to GA in the same change.
3. **OpenAI is the baseline, not the whole spec.** Anything it doesn't cover goes in explicit, documented extension fields.
4. **Shared code owns session/transport/events/capabilities; model dirs own encoder feeding and partial/final production.** No model-name branching in shared code (same rule as #1267).

## Requirements gathered from early users

These came from discussions with teams already building streaming STT servers on top of inference backends. They are recorded here in generalized form as design input.

**Transport and audio**
- One WebSocket per stream; PCM16 mono 16 kHz as the default input.
- Audio format is a negotiated session parameter, not a hard constant. Sample rate (8/16/24/48 kHz) and encoding (pcm16, µ-law, A-law) should be declarable; **8 kHz µ-law is a real need for telephony**, not a nice-to-have.
- Deployment topologies to support: co-located (server + model on one GPU box) and split (session/transport layer on CPU, model backend on separate GPUs). The protocol layer must not assume it lives in the same process as the model.

**Capability negotiation**
- On connect / `session.update`, the server declares what the loaded model can actually do, e.g. `partial_style`, `max_decode_window_s`, supported `input_format`s, `languages`, `segmentation_modes`, `concurrency`.
- `session.updated` reports **what was granted**, not an echo of the request. Clients cannot guess per-model behavior from outside, so this is the mechanism that makes "protocol first" work across a heterogeneous model set.

**Partial transcript semantics**
- `partial_style` must be declared explicitly (e.g. `append_only` vs `revising`). Several models (Whisper-style and Qwen3-ASR among them) revise earlier words as more context arrives; treating their output as append-only deltas is silently lossy. Clients need to know whether a delta may replace previously emitted text.

**Long input / buffer limits**
- Buffer overflow must not close the connection (no WS 1009 as the overflow response). A long turn should be split into multiple finals correlated by a turn id, so a session stays alive across arbitrary utterance lengths.

**Division of labour**
- VAD, turn policy, diarization and session admission are per-customer policy and typically live above us; we should make them optional / pluggable, not mandatory.
- What can

issues.title: MiniMax-Music3: dit_dav stage fails via device_mixin.set_device NotImplementedError, then "no NVIDIA driver" after workaround
issues.body:
Trying to serve MiniMax-Music3 (`sgl-omni serve --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-Music3 --port 8000`) on a real 2x A100-80GB instance (AWS, via Hugging Face Inference Endpoints, driver 580.159.03 / CUDA 13.0). Base environment: `hongccc/sglang-omni:dev`. Reproduced across multiple commits, including pinning to `05e268a` ("[Model] Support MiniMax Music 3 Model") — the very first commit that added MiniMax-Music3 support — so this isn't a recent regression, it appears to have never worked for this stage.

## Bug 1: `current_platform.set_device()` calls a stub that's documented as not-yet-active

```
File "sglang_omni/pipeline/stage_workers.py", line 581, in _construct_stage
    current_platform.set_device(int(gpu_id))
File ".../sglang/srt/platforms/device_mixin.py", line 180, in set_device
    raise NotImplementedError
NotImplementedError
```

`device_mixin.py`'s own docstring says `set_device` is `[Planned]`: "Reserved interface. SGLang core still uses hardcoded calls (e.g. `torch.cuda.set_device()`). OOT implementations will NOT take effect until the core is migrated in a future PR." So `stage_workers.py`'s `_construct_stage` (specifically for the `minimax_music3_dit_dav` process) is calling an interface that isn't backed yet — this reproduces even at commit `05e268a`, the first commit with MiniMax-Music3 support at all, so it isn't a later regression.

**Workaround applied**: monkey-patched `DeviceMixin.set_device` to call `torch.cuda.set_device()` directly (matching the documented interim behavior). Confirmed via traceback that the patch takes effect.

## Bug 2: after the patch, `torch.cuda.set_device()` reports "no NVIDIA driver" in this subprocess specifically

```
File ".../torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 638, in set_device
    torch._C._cuda_setDevice(device)
File ".../torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 478, in _lazy_init
    torch._C._cuda_init()
RuntimeError: Found no NVIDIA driver on your system. Please check that you have an NVIDIA GPU and installed a driver from http://www.nvidia.com/Download/index.aspx
```

This happens **only in the `minimax_music3_dit_dav` worker subprocess**. The parent process's `nvidia-smi` (run immediately before `sgl-omni serve` starts) correctly shows both A100-80GB GPUs. Tried:
- Explicitly setting `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1` / `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all` before `serve` starts (inherited by the child) — no effect, identical error.

Haven't been able to dig further — no interactive shell access into the live GPU instance (HF Inference Endpoints only exposes logs, not exec).

issues.title: [Evaluation] Stage MiniMax Music 3 serving-fidelity and signal-integrity qualification
issues.body:
## Motivation

This is an implementation tracker following the evaluation discussion in #1481. The goal is not to define one universal "music quality" score. It is to add the parts that are actionable for a serving runtime in two reviewable stages, while keeping subjective and heavyweight learned evaluation external.

I ran a preliminary offline signal-integrity pass over the 14 MiniMax Music 3 WAV files attached to #1481. The main observations were:

- 7/14 files reached or exceeded 0 dBTP under a 4x true-peak estimate.
- 27/28 channels carried a small positive DC offset (+0.0005 to +0.0015).
- 7/14 files reached the 750-frame output cap. This is not itself an error, but recording that the cap was reached would distinguish a bounded output from a model-selected ending.
- Click and silence detectors are content-sensitive: vinyl crackle, percussion, and intentional musical breaks can trigger them. These measurements should therefore remain diagnostics unless a model-specific policy is declared.

These findings do not determine whether the generated music is good. They identify measurable serving and signal properties and motivate the staged scope below.

## Stage 1: serving-fidelity qualification

**PR:** #1996

Add an opt-in MiniMax Music 3 GPU test next to `tests/test_model/test_qwen3_tts_batch_invariance.py`.

The test will cover:

1. Same-process repeatability for identical lyrics, caption, seed, and frame cap.
2. Repeatability across a clean server restart.
3. Batch invariance between serial batch-1 requests and concurrent requests under deterministic inference.
4. Positive execution evidence from model information or runtime statistics proving that the AR classifier-free-guidance rows were actually batched.

The hard assertion will be equality of decoded PCM for the controlled deterministic protocol. Attached reference WAV hashes will be report-only because a fixed hash may also pin the hardware, driver, and kernel stack.

This stage will be run on H100 before the PR is marked ready. A failure will be reported as a serving finding rather than hidden by weakening the comparison.

## Stage 2: reusable signal-integrity benchmark

**PR:** TBD

Add a small music evaluation path under `benchmarks/`, following the repository's existing dataset/task/metric organization and existing dependencies.

Proposed report-only measurements:

- decoded format, sample rate, channel count, frame count, and duration;
- whether generation reached the requested frame cap;
- peak and estimated true peak;
- clipped-sample count;
- per-channel DC offset;
- silent-window ratio and contiguous silence regions;
- stereo correlation;
- optional comparison with a matched reference run: exact PCM, aligned correlation, and NRMSE.

Synthetic CPU tests will cover the metric implementation. Model execution and reference comparisons will remain opt-in GPU benchmarks.

## Out of scope

- A universal automated music-quality pass/fail score.
- Genre-specific thresholds without validation data.
- Adding CLAP, MuQ-MuLan, Audiobox Aesthetics, SongEval, or other model weights to SGLang Omni CI.
- Treating FAD or any single learned metric as a merge gate.
- Human-listening infrastructure inside this repository.

Prompt alignment, aesthetics, distribution metrics, and blinded listening remain useful higher-level evaluation, but they answer model-quality questions rather than whether SGLang Omni served the model faithfully.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Stage 1 test is implement

issues.title: [Bug] MOSS-TD: batch-order nondeterminism splits one speaker on AISHELL4 long audio (delta_cer 0.23% to 1.15% in ~1 run in 5)
issues.body:
## Summary

On AISHELL4 long audio, MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize produces two stable outputs for the same input. In about one run in five it inserts an extra segment boundary and opens a new speaker id partway through a segment, which splits one reference speaker across two hypothesis speakers. The transcript text is unaffected, but cpCER for that sample goes from 4.9% to 25.1%, and the 20 sample stage aggregate `delta_cer` goes from about 0.23% to about 1.15%.

Decoding is greedy (temperature 0, set by #969). #959 measured 792/800 identical outputs across identical runs after that change, so roughly 1% residual nondeterminism was already known. This is that residual, landing on a sample where the diarization metric amplifies it.

## Evidence

One H100 pair, single MOSS-TD server per round, AISHELL4 long (20 samples), client concurrency 32, model revision unchanged across rounds. 15 consecutive rounds:

| rounds | AISHELL4 `delta_cer` | cpCER | DER |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 rounds | 0.175% to 0.236% | 14.06% to 14.08% | 9.59% to 9.84% |
| runs 5, 7, 14 | 1.138% to 1.149% | 14.98% to 15.00% | 10.17% to 10.38% |

A further 4 rounds on a later build produced no flip, so the observed rate is 3/19.

## What changes

Every flip is the same sample (`sample-000004`, a 38 minute meeting recording) at the same position, t = 34s. The text is nearly identical, `cer_no_spk` 4.87% against 4.85%; only the segmentation differs.

```
normal: ...明显的客流量也呃客流量也多了，呃咱这个销售这个呃营业额儿也上去了。[39.58][40.44][S01]
flip:   ...明显的客流量也[34.21][34.14][S06]呃客流量也多了，呃咱这个销售这个呃营业额儿也上去了。[39.54]
```

Because generation is autoregressive, every later segment that belonged to `S01` is then emitted as `S06`, and `S04` likewise becomes `S07`. Speaker count goes from 5 to 7. cpCER maps each reference speaker to exactly one hypothesis speaker, so the whole tail of that speaker scores as wrong.

## Root cause

Greedy decoding is deterministic given identical logits, but batch composition differs between rounds, so kernel shapes and reduction order differ and the logits carry small floating point differences. At t = 34s the two candidates, continue the current segment or emit a boundary plus a new speaker, are close enough that this is sufficient to flip the argmax. Timestamp values differ in their last digits throughout the output, from the same source.

## Why this matters

The ASR CI stage gates `AISHELL4_LONG_DELTA_CER_PERCENT_REF`. Any reference calibrated on non flipped rounds, including the current 0.318 on main, fails on a flipped round: the derived gate is 0.382 against an observed 1.15. Calibration cannot make this gate both meaningful and stable while the flip exists, which currently blocks the threshold work in #1896.

## Options

1. Set the reference high enough to cover the flip, about 1.15. The gate stays green but loses most of its power to detect a real diarization regression.
2. Replace `sample-000004` in the AISHELL4 CI subset. Cheapest path to a tight gate, but it hides a real behavior and another sample may do the same.
3. Make the segmentation decision robust, for example by not letting a near tie between a text token and a boundary token depend on batch shape. This is the real fix and the largest.

Reproduction: run the ASR CI stage 1 AISHELL4 long dataset repeatedly on one host and compare `per_sample` entries for `sample-000004` across rounds.

issues.title: [Bug] Audar-TTS unseeded requests inherit the previous request seed
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Audar-TTS reuses one `llama_cpp.Llama` instance across requests. A request with an explicit `seed` calls `llm.set_seed(seed)`, but a following request without a seed only calls `llm.reset()` and leaves the previous `_seed` in place.

`llama-cpp-python==0.3.34` is pinned by this repository. In that version, `Llama.reset()` clears token/model state but does not modify `_seed`; the sampler subsequently reads `self._seed`. Therefore an unseeded request is affected by an earlier user's explicit seed.

Expected: each unseeded request uses `LLAMA_DEFAULT_SEED`.

Actual: after a seeded request, the next unseeded request inherits that seed.

The minimal fix is to call `llm.set_seed(int(seed) if seed is not None else LLAMA_DEFAULT_SEED)` for every request.

### Reproduction

1. Create one Audar-TTS engine executor.
2. Send a request whose `AudarTTSState.generation_kwargs` contains `seed=23`.
3. Reuse the same executor for a second request whose generation kwargs omit `seed`.
4. Record calls to `Llama.set_seed`.

Current result: `[23]`.
Expected result: `[23, LLAMA_DEFAULT_SEED]`.

This is deterministic at the existing `create_tts_engine_executor()` unit-test seam using the repository's `FakeLlama`. The same `Llama` object is captured by the scheduler closure for both requests.

### Environment

- SGLang-Omni: main at `7989a5ed273587eb335a30f907235d1d1fbbf986`
- Declared dependency: `llama-cpp-python==0.3.34`
- Affected model: `audarai/Audar-TTS-V1-Turbo`
- Source path: `sglang_omni/models/audar_tts/stages.py`
- Host used for the dependency-free regression harness: macOS arm64, Python 3.14

The issue was confirmed against the pinned llama-cpp-python source contract and a deterministic FakeLlama regression at the actual executor seam. A real GGUF inference run was not performed on this host because the Audar optional dependencies and model are not installed.

issues.title: [Bug] Qwen3-TTS: `--enable_deterministic_inference true` makes every predictor CUDA-graph capture fail (`cublasCreate` inside capture) and still crashes under concurrency
issues.body:
### Checklist - [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help. - [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version. - [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback. - [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed. ### Describe the bug

With --enable_deterministic_inference true, the Qwen3-TTS talker's lazily captured code-predictor CUDA graph (sglang_model.py::_PredictorDecodeGraph._capture) fails on its first attempt for every (batch, 'sampled', top_k, …) key, and after 8 failures the predictor graph is disabled for the whole process:

[WARNING] sglang_omni.models.qwen3_tts.sglang_model: Disabling Qwen3-TTS predictor CUDA graph for key=(1, 'sampled', 50, False, False)
  File "sglang_omni/models/qwen3_tts/sglang_model.py", line 1745, in _predictor_o_proj_add_residual
    torch.addmm(residual_2d, attn_input, weight.t(), out=residual_2d)
RuntimeError: CUDA error: CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED when calling `cublasCreate(handle)`
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation failed due to a previous error during capture  (cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated)

Without the flag the same graphs capture cleanly (no such warning in ~20 non-deterministic soak runs on the same build), so this is specific to the deterministic path, which is the mode #1428 recommends for reproducible TTS output.

Root cause (fault 1) — confirmed with a standalone repro, no TTS model needed

Deterministic mode turns on SGLang's batch-invariant ops. enable_batch_invariant_mode() re-registers aten::mm, aten::addmm, aten::_log_softmax, aten::mean.dim, aten::rms_norm, aten::mm.dtype (and optionally aten::bmm) — but not the .out overloads.

_predictor_o_proj_add_residual has a Hopper-only fused path that is taken only while a stream is capturing (torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing() is one of the use_fused_addmm conditions) and calls torch.addmm(residual_2d, attn_input, weight.t(), out=residual_2d). That addmm.out call is the only place the process touches cuBLAS: the two warm-up forwards take the eager branch (o_proj(attn_input) → F.linear → batch-invariant GEMM), so cuBLAS is still uninitialised when capture begins, and the lazy cublasCreate happens inside torch.cuda.graph(...), which invalidates the capture. Warming up on the capture stream does not help (tested) because the warm-up never executes the fused branch.

The script in Reproduction below shows this without the model (1×H100, ~20 s):

batch-invariant mode on
F.linear (warmup path)   -> ['void deep_gemm::sm90_bf16_gemm_impl<...']        # batch-invariant kernel
torch.addmm (functional) -&

issues.title: TTS serving CI: batch32 latency gate is flaky by construction (p95 over 9 samples)
issues.body:
`TTS CI / stage 4 - serving stress` fails on unrelated PRs. The `batch32.latency_p95_s_max` gate takes p95 over only **9 samples**, so on that sample size p95 is effectively the max.

The `soak-300s` stage has a fat tail in passing runs too, so the gate passes or fails depending on which workload the tail happens to land on.

| run | soak median | soak p95 | soak p99 | share > 1.9825s | batch32 p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pass | 0.432 | 1.033 | 7.520 | 2.3% (12/512) | 0.952 |
| fail | 0.429 | 1.066 | 9.836 | 4.1% (21/512) | 10.192 |

The 9 batch32 latencies, same workload hash and same model in both runs:

* pass: 0.898 0.896 0.859 0.814 0.911 0.928 0.871 0.850 0.968
* fail: 0.914 0.822 2.186 0.864 0.902 **10.239 10.122 9.658** 1.017

The server is not slower: medians match, and 2126/2126 requests succeeded in the failing run with queue wait at 0.001s. Three of the nine batches simply landed in the tail.

Using the passing run's own 2.3% tail, P(at least one of 9 samples in the tail) is 19%; at 4.1% it is 31%.

Seen on #1049 and on `perf/code2wav-bounded-batching` (9.5 to 9.7s), both 3/3 attempts, so it is not PR specific.

Options: raise the sample count for `batch_32_all_valid`, gate on a median instead of a 9-sample p95, or set `SERVING_BATCH32_LATENCY_P95_S_REF` above the observed tail.

Sub-issue of #163 — focusing on reducing CPU overhead in the scheduler.

The scheduler has the following potential areas for optimization:

issues.title: [Feat] Shared TTS pipeline-state base + stage helpers
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. If the issue you raised is not a feature but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 2. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Motivation


### Motivation

The per-request state object that flows between pipeline stages is currently defined
per model, so its serialization and a few stage helpers are repeated across every TTS
model. `#512`'s `EncoderModelRunner` reads and writes this state, and would benefit from
a shared contract to type against. This issue extracts that small shared surface so
`#512` and future model integrations build on one base.
### Problem (evidence in current tree)

**No shared base for the per-request state.** Six standalone `@dataclass`es, zero
inheritance, each with its own `to_dict`/`from_dict`:

| Class | File | LOC |
|---|---|---|
| `HiggsTtsState` | `models/higgs_tts/payload_types.py` | 105 |
| `Qwen3TTSState` | `models/qwen3_tts/payload_types.py` | 106 |
| `MossTTSState` | `models/moss_tts/payload_types.py` | 110 |
| `S2ProState` | `models/fishaudio_s2_pro/payload_types.py` | 113 |
| `Qwen3OmniPipelineState` | `models/qwen3_omni/payload_types.py` | — |
| `LLaDA2UniPipelineState` | `models/llada2_uni/payload_types.py` | — |

The shared subset across them is small but identical: the token-usage triplet, the
decoded-audio tail, a repeated torch→list serialization helper, the
`load_state` / `store_state` wrappers in every `stages.py`, and a byte-for-byte
identical `_resolve_checkpoint` in four stage modules.

### Proposal

Add to two existing shared homes:

1. `scheduling/pipeline_state.py` — `PipelineStateBase` (common fields + generic
   `to_dict`/`from_dict` with an overridable `_serialize_value` tensor hook) + generic
   `load_state` / `store_state` / `build_usage`. Sits next to `SGLangARRequestData`.
2. `utils/checkpoint.py` — `resolve_checkpoint()`.

Model states subclass `PipelineStateBase` and declare only model-specific fields —
base owns the mechanism, subclass owns the semantics.

### Non-goals

- Don't unify input / generation params — they legitimately differ per model; the base
  covers only usage + audio tail.
- Keep each model's tensor-serialization policy via `_serialize_value`; behavior-check
  the migration rather than assuming byte-equivalence.

### Scope / task list

- [ ] Add `PipelineStateBase` + `load_state` / `store_state` / `build_usage` to `scheduling/pipeline_state.py`, and `resolve_checkpoint` to `utils/checkpoint.py`.
- [ ] Migrate Higgs first (reference per `#661`), accuracy-CI green; then roll out to the other TTS models.
- [ ] Type `#512`'s payload I/O against `PipelineStateBase`.

### Relationship to other issues

- **Unblocks `#512`**: gives `EncoderModelRunner` a stable state contract.
- **Serves `#493`**: same "base owns mechanism, model provides specifics" template, at the data layer.
- **Closes a `#661` gap**: removes ~300+ LOC of serialization/helper boilerplate.


### Related resources

_No response_

issues.title: [MOSS-TD] Limited same-GPU process-replica scaling with native CUDA MPS
issues.body:
## Summary

I tested `MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize` with one process replica and with two same-GPU process replicas using native CUDA MPS.

The original tested commit could not construct a Moss-TD process replica because the model factory did not accept `gpu_id`. The performance tests were run from a branch containing the minimal compatibility change required to enable replica placement and the benchmark sample filter used by the experiment.

- Test branch: https://github.com/stephenkgli/sglang-omni/tree/moss-td-process-replica-eval
- Test branch commit: `e1819ee7`

The results show that two replicas can improve peak throughput when client concurrency is high enough, but scaling remains substantially below 2x. Nsight Systems indicates that MPS makes the GPU busier, while request batching becomes fragmented across two independent schedulers.

## Test environment

- GPU: one NVIDIA H200
- Model: `OpenMOSS-Team/MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize`
- Dataset: `zhaochenyang20/movies800time`, validation split
- Benchmark path: end-to-end HTTP requests through `/v1/audio/transcriptions`
- Single-replica configuration: MPS off
- Dual-replica configuration:
  - two process replicas;
  - both replicas placed on the same physical GPU;
  - native CUDA MPS enabled;
  - strict round-robin request routing.

The validation split contains 800 samples. The primary performance runs excluded:

```text
sample-000237
sample-000318
```

Both samples exhibited runaway generation, producing tens of thousands of output characters and dominating the full-run wall time. The fixed-concurrency performance comparison therefore used the remaining 798 samples.

## Moss-TD configuration under test

Relevant Moss-TD defaults and runtime behavior:

| Component | Configuration |
|---|---|
| Decode CUDA graph | Enabled, with batch buckets captured up to batch size 96 |
| Prefill CUDA graph | Breakable CUDA graph enabled, with token buckets ranging from 1 to 4096 |
| Audio encoder CUDA graph | Enabled for dense audio chunk buckets 1-8 |
| Encoder batch size | `encoder_max_batch_size=2` |
| Encoder cache | 4 GiB per replica |
| Torch compile | Enabled, `torch_compile_max_bs=4` |
| Async decode | Enabled starting at batch size 1 |
| Request builders | 8 workers, at most 16 pending builds |
| Prefill admission coalescing | 4 requests or 12 ms |
| Sampling backend | PyTorch |
| Overlap schedule | Disabled |

With two replicas, these schedulers, CUDA graphs, encoder services, model states, and caches are instantiated independently in each process.

## Test methodology

Each server configuration was started fresh and primed before measurement.

The fixed server settings remained at:

```text
max_running_requests = 96 per replica
cuda_graph_max_bs = 96 per replica
```

Client concurrency was swept independently:

- Single replica: 16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96
- Two replicas + MPS: 16, 32, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128

Each point processed the complete filtered 798-sample set once. The sweep stopped after throughput passed its observed knee.

issues.title: [Roadmap] Multi-node Inference Support and Communication Enhancement
issues.body:
## Goal
The goal of this issue contains three main things:
* Get the current intra-node communication infra corect
* Get the communication topology clear
* Support high-efficiency multi-node inference

## Summary

sglang-omni today is a **single-host, multi-GPU** serving system. The whole-pipeline
deployment unit is one machine: process launch, control-plane endpoints, and the
default data relay all assume every stage lives on the same host.

For the next-gen omni model we are about to support, this is a common pipeline:

```
VAD/ASR → audio/video encoder → LLM backbone (200B+) → talker (TTS) → code2wav
```

The full pipeline does not fit on a single 8×H100 node. We therefore need to be able
to place **different stages on different physical nodes** and stream tensors between
them across the network.

More importantly, a key feature of Sglang-Omni is to solve the layout between process, stage and GPU, to disaggregate them and provide a clean implementation surface.  **Now we need to solve the topology between process, stage and <node,GPU>.**

---

## Design

### 1. Topology model: node / gpu / process / stage

Introduce **node** as the top placement coordinate and make GPU indices explicit as
`(node, local_gpu)`:

```
node (physical host)
  └── gpu (device, node-local index)
        └── process (OS process; owns ≤1 gpu on its node)
              └── stage-shard (one rank of one stage)
```

The **unit of placement is the stage-shard (rank)**, and every
shard has an address `(node_id, local_gpu_id)`. A *stage* is then a set of shards:

```
stage = [ shard_0, shard_1, ... shard_{tp_size-1} ]   # one shard per rank
shard_r  -->  process  -->  (node, gpu)
```

- Today, all shards of a stage share one node (intra-node TP). → single-node config.
- **Room for one-stage-multi-node:** because a shard's address is `(node, gpu)`, a
  stage's shards *can* later be spread across nodes (multi-node TP/PP) with **no schema
  redesign** — only the launcher/collective-init need to learn it (Phase 5). We design
  the placement plan in terms of per-shard `(node, gpu)` now so this stays a pure
  extension.

---

### 2. Communication protocols

There are **two classes** of traffic,

- **Class I — inter-stage edges** (the pipeline graph: A→B handoff, fan-in, streaming).
  Carried by the **relay** (bulk tensor data) plus the **control plane** (small
  signals). This is the omni-specific layer.
- **Class II — intra-stage parallelism** (within one stage's ranks: TP/EP collectives,
  PP point-to-point, leader→follower dispatch). Carried by **NCCL** and (today) local
  queues. This is mostly inherited from the model runner.

For each, we enumerate transport over the locality dimensions
**{same/diff gpu} × {same/diff node}** (process locality is derived: same-process is
only possible at same node + same gpu).

#### 2.1 Class I — inter-stage edge transport


| A→B locality                        | Control signal                    | Bulk + stream —**today**                                            | Bulk + stream —**target**                    |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| same process (⇒ same node+gpu)      | in-process                        | Python ref, zero-copy (`runtime.py:945-976`)                         | unchanged                                     |
| same node,**same gpu**, diff proces

issues.title: [Bug] POST /start_profile with an unknown trace_path_template placeholder crashes the entire serving pipeline
issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

### Summary

Passing a `trace_path_template` that contains any placeholder other than `{run_id}` / `{stage}` (e.g. `{pid}`, or even a stray `{`) to `POST /start_profile` raises an unguarded `KeyError` inside the stage process. The stage process dies, `mp_runner` detects the dead stage, and the **entire pipeline exits** — all in-flight requests are lost.

This contradicts the profiler's own documented discipline — ["Profiling must never break serving"](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/main/docs/developer_reference/profiler.md) — and is inconsistent with the event-recorder path a few lines below, which *is* exception-guarded.

### Context

Found while running the **model-profiling skill** introduced in [#1850](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/1850) (`.claude/skills/model-profiling/`) against Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct — the first omni-model run of that 5-layer runtime profiling methodology. Its Layer 1 (GPU busy ratio, kernel-timing method) drives `POST /start_profile` with a custom `trace_path_template`, which is exactly how the malformed placeholder reached the stage handler and took the server down mid-investigation. Per the methodology's own feedback loop, this pitfall has already been folded back into the skill's `METHODOLOGY.md` (§4, CUDA kernel-level profiling entry) so the next model's run won't hit it; the full profiling results will be posted separately as a sub-issue under the tracking issue [#1798](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/1798).

So this issue is the tooling-hardening fallout of that profiling run: the methodology assumes the profiler is safe to drive programmatically, and right now one bad template string breaks that assumption.

### Root cause

`Stage._on_profiler_start` formats the template with a fixed field set and no error handling:

```python
# sglang_omni/pipeline/stage/runtime.py:1792
base_tpl = msg.trace_path_template.format(run_id=run_id, stage=self.name)
```

Any other placeholder raises `KeyError` before `TorchProfiler.start()` runs. The event-recorder branch directly below (`runtime.py:1798-1808`) wraps its start in `try/except` and only logs a warning on failure, so the two profiler paths in the same function have asymmetric robustness.

### Observed failure (live server, Qwen3-Omni text-only)

Hit accidentally during the profiling run when a client passed `{pid}` in the template:

```text
2026-09-02 15:12:03,216 [ERROR] stage_workers.pipeline: Stage process pipeline failed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/root/sglang-omni/sglang_omni/pipeline/stage_workers.py", line 414, in stage_process_main
    _run_process(spec, ready_event, log)
  File "/root/sglang-omni/sglang_omni/pipeline/stage_workers.py", line 497, in _run_process
    asyncio.run(_start_and_run())
  ...
  File "/root/sglang-omni/sglan

issues.title: Sending a vocabulary hint to some ASR models silently does nothing
issues.body:
If you call `/v1/audio/transcriptions` with a `prompt` — the OpenAI-style field for "these words are likely in this audio" — two of the five ASR models accept the request, return 200, and never look at the field. Your vocabulary does nothing, and nothing tells you it did nothing.

Where each model stands today:

| model | what happens to your `prompt` |
|---|---|
| whisper_asr | works |
| moss_transcribe_diarize | works |
| qwen3_asr | dropped — fix in #1807 |
| fun_asr | dropped — it listens for a `hotwords` key that no caller can send; fix in #1874 |
| arkasr | this integration has no biasing mechanism, so there is nothing to wire yet — worth documenting |

Fun-ASR is the frustrating one. The hotword machinery inside it is complete and working; the HTTP field just never reaches it.

The other endpoint params are fine, checked so nobody has to re-audit: `language` reaches all five models. `task`, `detect_language` and `segment_timestamps` only mean something to whisper, and the endpoint checks capability before sending them. `temperature` and `stream` flow through the client.

## Proposal: a small test, not a refactor

Draft PR #1875 adds a contract test. Every key the endpoint can emit must be either consumed by each ASR model or declared unsupported with a one-line reason, and known gaps must name their fix PR and are re-checked so the list cannot rot. Both bugs above were silent; this makes the third one loud. It is a draft because the shape of the contract is the thing to review.

## Needs a decision, not just a patch

Only qwen3_asr and whisper_asr declare an `AudioChunkingConfig`. fun_asr, arkasr and moss_transcribe_diarize silently inherit the default, so how they treat long audio is something nobody actually chose. Writing down the current behaviour per model is a zero-change edit; deciding what each one *should* do is the discussion.

## Longer-term, parked here so it isn't lost

The five `prefill_coalesce_*` knobs are hand-threaded through about twenty engine-builder files, and several TTS models each privately accept both `instruct` and `instructions`. Both are consolidation candidates once the current wave settles. Neither is worth touching every model's signature right now.

## Non-goal for now

Shared base classes for ASR/TTS request builders. The models genuinely differ — whisper's timestamp machinery, fun_asr's ITN and hotwords, qwen3_asr's audio-token accounting — which matches the model-specific-first direction from the group discussion. The contract test above is the one cheap piece of that future abstraction we can have today.

Collaborated with Claude Code.

## Related

Checkpoint path resolution being done differently in every model family is the same theme — a capability the shared layer already has, adopted unevenly — and is tracked separately in #1877, with the first migrated batch in #1878.

issues.title: [Docs] Standardize Documentation Structure and Cookbook Format
issues.body:
## 1. Motivation & Goals

As SGLang-Omni scales, model cookbooks have become bloated with redundant API references, deployment tuning, benchmark dumps, and internal implementation details. 

**Objective:** Align SGLang-Omni's documentation grammar with SGLang-main while preserving multimodal-specific abstractions (multi-stage pipelines, audio/streaming protocols, speech APIs, hardware qualification).

---

## 2. Core Principles

1. **Cookbook = Operational Recipe:** Focus strictly on *how to deploy and run a specific model*. Move generic runtime features, API specs, and deep benchmark analysis to shared docs.
2. **Single Source of Truth:** Shared runtime behaviors (e.g., streaming, admission control, CUDA graphs) live in central guides; cookbooks document only model-specific deviations/overrides.
3. **Docs Explain; Examples Execute:** Reference checked-in configs (`examples/configs/...`) rather than embedding duplicate, unverified configs in markdown.
4. **Verified Hardware Only:** State verified/tested hardware (e.g., `Validated: RTX 4090 24GB`) rather than unverified theoretical minimums.

---

## 3. Proposed Information Architecture

```text
docs/
├── get_started/          # Installation, quickstart, hardware overview, release notes
├── user_guide/
│   ├── serving/          # Public API contracts (/v1/audio/*, /v1/chat/*, streaming, errors)
│   ├── advanced_features/# Shared runtime capabilities (MPS/DP, CUDA graph, offload, batching)
│   ├── deployment/       # Multi-stage sizing, stage placement, memory tuning, multi-GPU
│   └── supported_models/ # Centralized model support & capability matrices
├── cookbook/             # Model-specific operational recipes (tts/, asr/, omni/, generation/)
├── benchmarks/           # Methodology, metrics, reproducibility, and qualification reports
├── developer_guide/      # Architecture, stage interfaces, pipeline lifecycle, extensions
└── references/           # Configuration reference, CLI parameters, error codes
```

---

## 4. Standard Model Cookbook Template

Every model cookbook must follow this minimal, consistent structure:

````markdown
# <Model Name>

<One-sentence description of the model and its primary use case.>

## At a Glance

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| **Task** | TTS / ASR / Omni / Music / Generation |
| **Checkpoint(s)** | `<org/repo-id>` |
| **Endpoint(s)** | `/v1/...` |
| **Pipeline** | `stage_1` → `stage_2` → `stage_3` |
| **Input / Output** | Text / Audio / Multimodal |
| **Streaming** | Yes / No / Partial |
| **Validated Hardware**| 1× RTX 4090 (24 GB) |
| **Support Status** | CI tested / Performance qualified / Experimental |

## Installation
Model-specific dependencies only (do not repeat generic install steps).

## Deployment

### Recommended Configuration
```bash
sgl-omni serve --model-path <path> --config examples/configs/<model>.yaml
```

### Other Validated Configurations
*(Optional: consumer GPU, multi-GPU, or low-memory configs.)*

## Quickstart Request

### curl
```bash
curl http://localhost:30000/v1/... -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{...}'
```

### Python
```python
# Minimal working snippet
```

## Model-Specific Capabilities & Configuration
- Document model-specific parameters (e.g., voice cloning, language hints, diarization).
- Document overrides to runtime defaults (do not duplicate the full config reference).

## Limitations
- Concrete unsupported features or runtime constraints.

## Benchmarking
```bash
python -m benchmarks.eval.<script> --model

issues.title: Track _CountingInbox claim invariant for future immediate-drain support
issues.body:
## Context

#611 introduces `_CountingInbox` in `ThreadedSimpleScheduler` to track `new_request` IDs across the queue-to-dispatch handoff.

`_CountingInbox._get()` moves a request ID from queued counts to claimed counts. The current scheduler dispatch loop pairs that with `release_claim()` in a `finally` block, so normal dispatch keeps the accounting balanced.

## Current status

This is not a current production issue:

- `pyproject.toml` supports Python `<3.13`
- no production path currently calls `Queue.shutdown(immediate=True)` or another immediate-drain API on this inbox
- normal scheduler dispatch pairs every dequeued `new_request` with `release_claim()`

## Future invariant

If the project later supports Python 3.13+ or adds an immediate-drain/shutdown path for this queue, that path must preserve `_CountingInbox` accounting.

Specifically, every dequeued `new_request` must either reach the dispatch `finally` path, or the drain/shutdown path must explicitly clear or reconcile `_claimed_counts`.

Otherwise, stale claimed IDs could make `is_reachable()` return true permanently and route later aborts into `_queued_aborts`.

## Related

- #611
- Review discussion: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/pull/611#discussion_r3663333909

issues.title: [Roadmap] Consumer GPU support for ASR and TTS serving
issues.body:
## Summary

SGLang-Omni is primarily developed and validated on datacenter GPUs, while many supported ASR and TTS models are small enough to run on consumer hardware. This roadmap tracks support for single-GPU colocated ASR/TTS serving on Linux.

The first target is one RTX 4090 (Ada, SM89, 24 GB). RTX 5090 (consumer Blackwell, SM120, 32 GB) remains a later architecture-compatibility target, but the initial implementation and validation should start from a single RTX 4090.
All stages of a supported pipeline should run colocated on the same GPU. Tensor parallelism, multi-GPU stage placement, consumer-specific router work, RTX 5090 NVFP4 optimization, Windows/WSL2, and dedicated consumer-GPU CI are out of scope for this roadmap.
## Why this is needed

Current defaults contain assumptions inherited from H100/H200/B200-class systems:
- `flash-attn-4` is a required dependency even though it targets Hopper and Blackwell rather than Ada.
- Some model paths default to FA3 or use legacy FlashAttention APIs.
- Some FP8/CUTLASS paths only recognize SM90/SM100.
- Default concurrency, CUDA Graph batch sizes, KV-cache allocation, encoder caches, and static memory fractions are sized for high-memory GPUs.
- Model compatibility is often inferred from weight size even though KV cache, CUDA Graph pools, compile workspaces, codecs/vocoders, request state, and fragmentation determine the real peak.
RTX 4090 is SM89 and RTX 5090 is SM120; SM120 is not equivalent to B200/SM100. They need architecture-appropriate kernels and separate memory validation.

Hardware references: [RTX 4090](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/graphics-cards/40-series/rtx-4090/), [RTX 5090](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/graphics-cards/50-series/rtx-5090/), and [CUDA compute capability](https://developer.nvidia.com/cuda-gpus).
## User and platform assumptions
- Linux is the supported host platform for this roadmap.
- The primary user has one 24 GB RTX 4090.
- The target workload is local development, evaluation, and low-to-moderate-concurrency serving.
- Every supported model must run as a complete colocated pipeline on one GPU.
- Existing router work is tracked separately in [[Roadmap] Router & Same-GPU DP #921](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/issues/921). No consumer-specific router changes are planned unless a concrete incompatibility is discovered.
- RTX 5090 is validated after the RTX 4090 path is functional; it must use SM120-compatible kernels rather than inheriting SM100 assumptions.
## Goals
- [ ] Install and start SGLang-Omni on a single RTX 4090 without requiring an unusable architecture-specific kernel.
- [ ] Support BF16/FP16 colocated serving within 24 GB where the complete model pipeline fits.
- [ ] Extend the same capability-based design to a single RTX 5090 without assuming SM120 equals SM100.
- [ ] Select attention, GEMM, MoE, and quantization backends from runtime capabilities rather than GPU name strings.
- [ ] Fall back to a compatible backend or fail at startup with an actionable error.
- [ ] Provide conservative 24 GB and 32 GB memory profiles using existing server arguments.
- [ ] Publish reproducible correctness, quality, stability, memory, and performance results.
- [ ] Provide documented launch configurations for validated models.
## Non-goals
- Tensor parallelism, including TP2 and TP4.
- Multi-GPU stage placement or pipeline parallelism.
- Consumer-specific data-parallel/router work.
- RTX 5090 NVFP4 optimization.
- Windows or WSL2 supp

issues.title: [Qwen3-TTS] Make speech-tokenizer loading stage- and variant-aware
issues.body:
## Motivation

Qwen3-TTS currently loads a full speech tokenizer into the Talker stage for every model variant, while the vocoder stage also owns a speech tokenizer for decoding generated speech codes.

That is necessary for `Base`, but not for `CustomVoice` or `VoiceDesign` on the Talker side.

The important distinction is that **CustomVoice and VoiceDesign still need speech-tokenizer decoding in the vocoder**. What they do not need is the separate Talker-side tokenizer copy used for reference-audio encoding.

This is not just a current SGLang-Omni request-path limitation. It follows the upstream Qwen3-TTS model capability split:

- `Base` supports voice cloning from reference audio. Upstream `create_voice_clone_prompt()` uses `model.speech_tokenizer.encode(...)` to produce reference speech codes, and `generate_voice_clone()` is gated to `tts_model_type == "base"`.
- `CustomVoice` conditions on a predefined speaker ID, plus optional instruction text. Its generation API does not accept reference audio.
- `VoiceDesign` conditions on natural-language voice/style instructions. Its generation API does not accept reference audio.
- All three variants still need speech-code decoding after Talker generation, which is why the vocoder-side tokenizer remains required.

Conceptually:

```text
Base
reference audio
    -> speech tokenizer encode
    -> reference speech codes
    -> Talker
    -> generated speech codes
    -> vocoder speech tokenizer decode
    -> waveform

CustomVoice
text + predefined speaker (+ optional instruction)
    -> Talker
    -> generated speech codes
    -> vocoder speech tokenizer decode
    -> waveform

VoiceDesign
text + natural-language voice description
    -> Talker
    -> generated speech codes
    -> vocoder speech tokenizer decode
    -> waveform
```

## Current SGLang-Omni behavior

The Talker builder historically loads a full speech tokenizer unconditionally. The vocoder then loads another tokenizer for decode.

For `CustomVoice` and `VoiceDesign`, the Talker-side copy has no reference-encoding role, so it becomes redundant fixed GPU residency.

The safe ownership rule should therefore be:

| Variant | Talker tokenizer encode needed? | Vocoder tokenizer decode needed? |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Base | yes | yes |
| CustomVoice | no | yes |
| VoiceDesign | no | yes |
| unknown / future variant | keep historical behavior | yes |

Unknown or future model types should conservatively keep the Talker tokenizer until their capability contract is known.

## Implementation

PR #1870 implements the narrow first step:

- skip the Talker-side speech-tokenizer load only for known non-reference variants (`CustomVoice` and `VoiceDesign`)
- preserve the existing behavior for `Base`
- preserve the existing behavior for unknown/future model types
- keep the vocoder tokenizer unchanged

This intentionally does not introduce partial encoder/decoder loading or change reference preprocessing ownership.

## Validation

H200 fixed-KV A/B validation for PR #1870 showed:

- Talker + vocoder tokenizer loads: `2 -> 1`
- ready GPU residency: `-318 MiB`
- post-request GPU residency: `-276 MiB`
- KV capacity unchanged, because the Talker tokenizer loads after KV-pool sizing
- fixed single-request CustomVoice output: byte-identical WAV SHA256 in both AB and BA comparisons
- zero request failures

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`RealtimeSession` rejects three client-controlled values with a bare `assert`
(`sglang_omni/serve/realtime/session.py`):

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/627e74b8c01bfce3e2cec4d1b0a39adc695f68e8/sglang_omni/serve/realtime/session.py#L160-L161 

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/627e74b8c01bfce3e2cec4d1b0a39adc695f68e8/sglang_omni/serve/realtime/session.py#L165-L166

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/627e74b8c01bfce3e2cec4d1b0a39adc695f68e8/sglang_omni/serve/realtime/session.py#L197

None of these is a server-side invariant. Each is a value the WebSocket client picks: the shape of
the frame, the `type` field, and a `session.update` parameter.

**What happens.** Neither `run()` nor `dispatch()` catches anything, and the endpoint wraps the
session in `try/finally` with no `except` (`sglang_omni/serve/openai_api.py`, `_register_realtime`):

```python
await websocket.accept()
session = manager.open(websocket)
try:
    await session.run()
finally:
    await manager.close(session.session_id)
```

So an `AssertionError` reaches the ASGI layer, which closes the connection. The client gets no
`error` event explaining what it did wrong, and the session loses any buffered audio. A typo in
`type`, or one stray non-object frame, ends the session instead of being reported.

The third case needs nothing unusual from the client, because the session schema advertises the
values that trip it (`sglang_omni/serve/realtime/events.py`):

```python
input_audio_format: Literal["pcm16", "g711_ulaw", "g711_alaw"] | None = None
```

A client that reads the schema and sends `g711_ulaw` gets its socket closed with no explanation.

**The same message already rejects the sibling field properly.** This file uses `send_error` for
`unsupported_modality`, `invalid_content_index`, `item_not_found`, and, on the line immediately
below the third assert, for the output audio format:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-omni/blob/627e74b8c01bfce3e2cec4d1b0a39adc695f68e8/sglang_omni/serve/realtime/session.py#L198-L204

One `session.update` message, two different contracts for the same class of mistake.

**A second, latent failure mode.** `python -O` strips the asserts. Two of the three then fall through
into a more confusing downstream exception, and the third silently succeeds:

| value | default interpreter | `python -O` |
|---|---|---|
| non-object frame | `AssertionError` | `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'` in `parse_client_event` |
| unrecognized `type` | `AssertionError` | `KeyError: <class 'NoneType'>` on the `HANDLERS` lookup |
| `input_audio_format: g711_ulaw` | `AssertionError` | **`session.updated` granting `g711_ulaw`** |

Nothing in this repository runs `python -O` today, so this mode is latent rather than an active
production bug. The last row is t

issues.title: [Comm] Record the failure paths, and run a soak when the comm layer changes
issues.body:
## English

### Summary

This issue asks for two things.

**First, trace events on the paths that fail.** The comm data plane emits eight events today. All eight record success. The layer emits nothing when a transfer fails. It emits nothing when it keeps slots after a failure. It emits nothing when it keeps a pending entry after a failure. If any of these happen in production, the logs show nothing.

We scoped this to four events on the slot-pool path when we opened the issue. Since then we read the paged KV path and found a larger gap, described below. #1595 implements the KV part.

**Second, a soak that runs only when the comm layer changes.** We ran one for 8 hours and it answered a question that no unit test answers: does the layer leak resources under sustained load? A soak costs a GPU for hours, so it must not run on every pull request. It should run when a pull request touches `sglang_omni/comm/` or `sglang_omni/relay/`.

The two parts connect. The soak reads the trace events. Without events on the failure paths, a soak can only report that nothing crashed.

Neither part changes behaviour. Neither part asks you to choose a recovery policy.

### The paged KV path has no events at all

The eight events all sit on the slot-pool path. Paged KV transfer uses pre-registered pools and page indices instead of slots, so none of them fire for it. We checked every function: thirteen functions across `comm/engine.py` and `relay/cuda_ipc.py`, about 500 lines, contain no `_comm_trace` call. `send_kv_pages` is 113 lines, `get_kv_pages` is 108, `prepare_kv_receive` is 58, and none of them record anything.

`get_kv_pages` also constructs its operation with `emit_trace=False`, so the one place where an existing event could have fired is switched off.

Prefill/decode disaggregation will run its traffic over this path. Today that traffic would produce no log line, on success or on failure.

Two smaller gaps sit next to it.

**The router never records which transport an edge selected.** An edge that falls back keeps working, so every counter still reads as healthy. We lost an eight-hour soak to this: one edge moved from `cuda_ipc` to `shm` after the first request, the run reported balanced ACK counts and flat memory, and the path under test carried no traffic. Nothing in the log said so.

**The direct-IPC stream path records only its sender.** `send_stream_chunk` and `_run_stream_send` emit; `outbound_stream` and `read_stream_chunk` do not. That path has no byte ceiling, and measuring the held bytes needs both rates, so the missing consumer event makes the growth unmeasurable.

#1595 adds fourteen events for these three gaps and keeps them behind the same environment variable. The four events in Part 1 below still apply to the slot-pool path and are not covered by that pull request.

### Why to add the events now

Two pieces of work will soon need data that the layer cannot produce today.

**Paged KV transfer.** #1315 and #1382 are merged. No pipeline code calls them yet. When some code does call them, the plane will carry a second kind of allocation. Those allocations use pages, not slots. They are much larger than today's per-token traffic. If you add the events first, the first integration starts with a baseline.

**Cross-node relay.** #862 Phase 3 states that the data plane must prove itself before the orchestration layer depends on it. A proof needs the same measurements on every transport. The eight events already have the right shape. They on

issues.title: [MOSS TTS Realtime] Preserve codec decoder state across turns
issues.body:
talk110 is one continuous ACL6060 benchmark talk, not 194 independent conversations. InfiniSST translated it online and emitted 194 Chinese text chunks. We sent each chunk to MOSS-TTS-Realtime as one TTS turn so its audio could be played immediately. All 194 turns belong to the same logical speaker session. The boundary under test is therefore an application-level streaming turn boundary, not a session boundary.

PR #1410 preserves the acoustic model history across successful turns, but the vocoder state still ends at each turn. It keeps one process-wide codec.streaming context, then leases one codec slot to each request. When a turn finishes, decode_delta drains the pending frames and releases the slot. _CodecStreamSession.release resets that slot, so the next turn in the same session starts with fresh causal codec state.

We verified the effect with this 194 turn talk. The audio codes were generated once, then the same 8,581 frames were decoded in two ways. Resetting the decoder at every turn caused clear speaker changes. Keeping one decoder context for the full talk was noticeably more consistent in human A/B. Both outputs were 686.48 seconds and 16,475,520 samples.

Turn completion should emit all pending PCM without resetting the session-owned codec slot. The slot should be released on session close, TTL expiry, abort, or failure. Different sessions must remain isolated.

A regression test can run two turns with one session_id and verify that codec state continues across the boundary. A new session or a closed session should start fresh. The fixed-code service output can also be compared with one continuous codec decode.

Reproduction and report:

https://github.com/luojiaxuan/S2S_omni/blob/a2eb237/docs/moss_realtime_codec_context_issue.md

https://github.com/luojiaxuan/S2S_omni/blob/a2eb237/scripts/codec_decoder_context_ab.py

https://github.com/luojiaxuan/S2S_omni/blob/a2eb237/projects/infinisst_moss_tts_cascade/artifacts/codec_decoder_context_ab_talk110/report.json

This applies to #1410. It is separate from #801, which tracks codec state correctness and CUDA graphs inside one streaming request.

issues.title: [Tracking][Pipeline] Process-level replicas
issues.body:
## Summary

This issue tracks the implementation and productionization of process-level replicas in the SGLang-Omni pipeline runtime.

## Motivation

Replicating the entire pipeline applies the same data-parallel configuration to every process, even when only one part of the pipeline is saturated. This can duplicate unnecessary model state and leave CPU cores or GPUs underutilized. Process-level replicas provide finer-grained data parallelism by allowing each process group to scale independently according to its workload and available resources.

## Existing work

- #1131 defines the original runtime-level stage-replica design and the Qwen3-Omni performance target.
- #1175 implements stage-level replica expansion, request-sticky round-robin binding, binding propagation, logical target resolution, and the initial Qwen3-Omni deployment.
- #1262 is a draft follow-up for replicated entry stages and logical source normalization at fan-in and streaming boundaries.
- #1276 record Higgs TTS replica benchmark results and documentation.

## TODO

1. **Replace stage-level replicas with process-level replicas.**  
   Replicate a complete process group instead of expanding each stage independently. Stages and TP ranks within the same process should share one replica identity and request binding while preserving local state and process topology.

2. **Support replicated entry stages.**  
   Allow the entry stage to belong to a replicated process group. The Coordinator should select a concrete entry replica during admission and verify that all configured entry replicas are ready before serving requests.

3. **Support fan-in from replicated stages.**  
   Model-facing fan-in APIs should continue using logical stage names even when data comes from a physical replica such as `encoder@r1`. Transport routing, ACKs, ordering, and observability should retain the physical replica identity.

4. **Validate compatibility across model pipelines.**  
   Test process-level replicas across representative TTS, multimodal, and TP-enabled pipelines, covering startup, inference, streaming, abort, output parity, and performance. Track each discovered incompatibility in a child issue and fix runtime-generic problems in the framework.

5. **Add request-hash cache-affinity routing.**  
   Add a deterministic routing policy that sends requests sharing reusable context to the same replica, using a stable session or prefix/cache key rather than only a unique request ID. Compare its cache-hit rate, latency, throughput, and load balance against round-robin routing.

6. **Add metrics and tooling for automated performance tuning.**  
   Expose machine-readable per-process and per-replica metrics such as queue depth, in-flight requests, service time, batch size, throughput, tail latency, cache-hit rate, CPU/GPU utilization, and memory pressure. Provide profiling, benchmarking, and configuration-search tools so future autotuners can optimize replica counts, placement, routing policies, and runtime parameters for the best workload-specific performance.

issues.title: [Perf] Extend MOSS-TTS Delay sampling CUDA Graph to feedback embedding
issues.body:
PR: #1792 
## Motivation

MOSS-TTS Delay still leaves one repeat-per-decode-step operation eager after the existing sampling CUDA Graph in #1303: feedback embedding for the sampled 33-channel row.

This is a direct follow-up to the MOSS-TTS optimization tracker #1233, under the **AR sampling** workstream. The earlier profiling investigation #1232 identified launch-heavy eager sampling/feedback work outside the backbone CUDA Graph as the dominant AR-side optimization direction; #1303 captured sampling and Delay-FSM updates, but feedback embedding intentionally remained eager.

Current decode flow is effectively:

```text
backbone decode CUDA Graph
  -> eager LM heads
  -> sampling CUDA Graph (#1303)
  -> eager feedback embedding
  -> next decode step
```

The feedback embedding path performs 33 embedding lookups plus sequential accumulation through `_prepare_multi_modal_inputs(rows)` on every decode step.

## Qualification results

A self-contained timing probe on H200 measured feedback embedding at roughly **1.5-2.0 ms per decode step**, about one third of the measured `decode_collect` GPU time in the sampled c8/c16 runs. The cost scaled weakly with batch size, consistent with a launch/latency-heavy path rather than a throughput-efficient batched kernel.

A diagnostic CUDA Graph that captured only feedback embedding passed exact `torch.equal` checks for the captured batch buckets. This diagnostic is not the proposed production design.

For service-level validation, the benchmark methodology was first calibrated with a true A/A null control. The final protocol uses two exclusive H200s simultaneously, explicit CPU-core partitioning, warm reference caches, and physical-GPU crossover so fixed GPU-speed differences cancel.

Null control, c16, 192 warmup + 192 measured samples, 4 rounds:

| Metric | Crossover effect |
| --- | ---: |
| QPS | -0.41% |
| Audio throughput | -0.41% |
| Mean latency | -0.50% |
| Mean RTF | -0.51% |
| ITL | +0.19% |

The null also exposed an approximately 2.5 percentage-point physical-GPU difference, which the crossover estimator cancels.

Diagnostic feedback-graph A/B, same protocol, 8 rounds:

| Metric | Crossover effect | Placement consistency |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| QPS | **+1.29%** | +0.71% / +1.87% |
| Audio throughput | **+1.30%** | +0.70% / +1.90% |
| Mean latency | **+1.24%** | +0.67% / +1.81% |
| Mean RTF | **+1.24%** | +0.65% / +1.83% |
| TTFC | +0.20% | near flat, as expected |
| ITL | **+7.99%** | +7.34% / +8.64%, 8/8 wins |

Mean generated audio duration was identical between arms in both the null and candidate runs.

The strongest evidence is the ITL result: the optimization targets repeated decode-step feedback work, and the improvement is large, consistent across both physical GPU placements, and absent from the null control. The smaller end-to-end QPS/latency gain is directionally consistent but should be revalidated on the production-shaped implementation before making a final performance claim.

## Proposed implementation

Do **not** upstream the standalone diagnostic graph or add a second graph manager.

Instead, extend the existing MOSS-TTS sampling CUDA Graph from #1303 so the captured graph produces both:

1. `DelaySamplingOutput` / sampled `rows`
2. feedback embeddings derived from those rows via `_prepare_multi_modal_inputs`

Conceptually:

```text
existing sampling CUDA Graph
  -> Delay sampling / FSM
  -> rows
  -> feedback embedding
  -> replay returns rows + feedback embeddings
```
